**Set `activationMode="manual"` on the view tabs. Arrow keys currently trigger router navigation.**
Radix Tabs defaults to `activationMode="automatic"`. In that mode, moving focus to a trigger with an arrow key calls `onValueChange` at once.
`handleViewChange` calls `router.push` whenever the target view needs a different window. Week → Month and Week → Day are examples. A keyboard user who presses ArrowRight on "Week" therefore starts a navigation before choosing a view.
The new window changes the `DiaryPageClient` key, so the toolbar remounts. Focus leaves the tab list. This breaks keyboard navigation between the Day, Week, Month and List tabs.
With manual activation, arrow keys only move focus. Enter or Space selects the view.

**Restore focus to the trigger after the dialog closes. Removing `DialogTrigger` drops focus return.**
Radix `DialogContent` handles `onCloseAutoFocus` by calling `preventDefault()` and then focusing `context.triggerRef.current`. Only `DialogTrigger` fills `triggerRef`.
This plain `Button` is outside `DialogTrigger`, so `triggerRef` stays `null`. After Cancel, Escape or a successful submit, focus goes to `document.body`. Keyboard and screen-reader users lose their place in the Diary header.
The trigger also no longer gets the `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded` attributes that `DialogTrigger` added.
